title: Two performances that differ only in delivery
statement: To teach how performance shapes meaning, have learners compare two performances of one scene, judge what each delivery does to a character and support it with the words.
detail: One unit's design makes its third lesson the first use of video for teaching, with the option of two videos that present the lead character as a confident leader or a vulnerable outsider, and specifies an oral comparison of two performances. Review set the task as hear the difference, locate the words that support it, then explain the interpretation. The illustrated-film design then proposed one scene with two deliveries, confident and vulnerable, so students hear how performance changes interpretation.
against: It was offered as an option and not built or tried with students. Which productions to license is still undecided (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 312). No large randomized controlled trial isolates side-by-side comparison of two productions as a technique (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/video-03-shakespeare-performance-video.md`, line 50), and the role method is a practitioner account without measured outcomes (line 25). Every published licence found grants platform viewing, "not clip extraction or embedding in another app" (`g9/library/collections/g3-repo-initiative-g9-othello-2026-10-01/research/VIDEO-SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 33-34).

evidence.quote: There is the option to generate two videos there, so students can see whether Othello is presented as a confident leader or a vulnerable outsider.
